subject: Aligning on SLO measurement, reporting cadence, and remedies for DataFlow PoC
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Carlos Montoya <carlos.montoya@dataflowanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Aligning on SLO measurement, reporting cadence, and remedies for DataFlow PoC

Hi Carlos —

Great to chat earlier. Quick recap from our call and a proposed next-steps checklist so we can scope the PoC and the SLA language:

Primary targets we discussed
- Non-streaming text generation: p95 latency <= 200 ms (server-side, measured at token generation request-to-first-token).
- Streaming first-byte latency: <= 250 ms for 95th percentile; steady-state chunk delivery should not exceed 50 ms inter-chunk on average for long streams.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline 500 req/s, sustained concurrency ~50 concurrent sessions; burst to 200 for short windows (<=1 minute).
- Availability: 99.9% regional availability objective (we'll define measurement windows below).

Measurement & reporting (proposed)
- Measurement window: 5-minute sliding windows aggregated to hourly and daily roll-ups.
- Percentiles: report p50/p95/p99 for both server-latency and end-to-end (if we instrument client-side).
- Exclusions: warm-up, scheduled maintenance windows (we'll enumerate in SLA), customer-induced throttling (your client limits), and synthetic-load tests.
- Reporting cadence: weekly automated SLO reports (token-level breakdown, cost-per-1000 tokens, model variant used), monthly executive summary, and an on-demand export (CSV/Parquet) via console.

Remedies & fallbacks (high level)
- Automated fallback to compatible smaller model variant on capacity constraints + routing to cross-region replica as primary mitigation.
- Remedies: service credits capped at 10% of monthly invoice for sustained SLO violations (we can refine language). Redwood prefers operational fallbacks over monetary-only remedies; we can propose specific failover mappings in the draft.

Action items I propose (can you confirm?):
1) Confirm the two measurement definitions you prefer: server-side (Redwood probes at the edge) vs end-to-end (your client instrumented). If you want end-to-end to be the contractual metric, we'll need SRE-level visibility on your client instrumentation.
2) Share any latency SLAs you already track internally and a sample query set/streaming workloads so we can run calibrated tests.
3) Introduce your SRE/Perf contact (cc Linda?) so we can schedule a technical sync with Marissa (implementation lead) and Ben (solutions).

Attached: SLO worksheet (dfa-slo-worksheet.xlsx) and an outline of proposed SLA term language (redwood-sla-term-outline-v1.pdf). Also linking the HubSpot deal and the perf test plan.

If helpful, we can draft two SLA variants: one that uses server-side measurement (simpler, Redwood reports) and one that uses end-to-end (requires client instrumentation but may better reflect user experience). Which would you prefer for the PoC?

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: dfa-slo-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-sla-term-outline-v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Carlos Montoya <carlos.montoya@dataflowanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Linda Zhao <linda.zhao@dataflowanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aligning on SLO measurement, reporting cadence, and remedies for DataFlow PoC

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap and the worksheet. A few clarifications from our side before we schedule the tech sync: 

1) Measurement: our primary preference is an end-to-end user-experience metric (we've seen server-side-only metrics miss client-network variability). That said, for the PoC we could accept server-side as the initial contractual metric if we can get p99 on end-to-end for our internal monitoring. Can you outline what instrumentation you need on our side to make end-to-end contractual?

2) Percentiles: for streaming workloads we care a lot about tail behavior — can we see p99 for first-byte latency and p99 inter-chunk gaps? p95 is fine for non-streaming.

3) Throughput & burst: the numbers look reasonable. Our initial expected sustained workload is closer to 300 req/s with spikes to 1200 for short batch runs; can Redwood support a burst model that auto-throttles gracefully or do we need reserved capacity?

4) Remedies: we prefer engineered mitigations first (automatic failover to a fallback model or region) and only then a monetary credit. Credits are OK but only as a backstop. Also want to understand how Redwood measures root cause (infra vs model-quality vs client-side) for applying remedies.

Procurement note: we are on a 60-day procurement timeline and need a draft SLA and an estimate for reserved capacity costs to include in our internal recommendation.

I'll loop Linda (SRE) — she can share sample stream traces and a short corpus for latency testing.

Regards,
Carlos Montoya
VP Engineering, DataFlow Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Aligning on SLO measurement, reporting cadence, and remedies for DataFlow PoC

Forwarding Carlos' notes — good clarifications. Karthik / Ben, please see my suggested split of responsibilities so we can respond quickly: 

- Marissa (Services/Product): draft two SLA stubs (server-side metric vs end-to-end) with explicit exclusions and a remediation ladder (failover -> traffic shaping -> credits). Include clear definitions for warm-up, scheduled maintenance, and customer-induced throttling.
- Ben (Solutions/Commercial): produce reserved capacity cost ballpark and an option for on-demand burst allowances (pricing tiers + how long burst is supported).
- Karthik (AE): coordinate procurement timeline and get Linda invited to the perf sync.

Notes on measurement: for end-to-end we should request a lightweight client SDK snippet (1-2 endpoints) that can emit traces or use the existing X-Request-ID header to correlate. That should be enough for contractual acceptance if Linda confirms sampling coverage.

I'll aim to have a first-pass SLA wordings and the remediation ladder by EOD Thu (19 Nov). Karthik, can you nudge Carlos for the sample traces and confirm the spike profile?

Marissa Cole
Head of Services, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aligning on SLO measurement, reporting cadence, and remedies for DataFlow PoC

Thanks — confirming Linda will share a 10-minute sample trace set and a 1k-message corpus by EOD tomorrow. We can also provide a short list of production-like prompt templates for streaming tests.

On the measurement preference: we'll accept server-side for the initial PoC contract if Redwood can commit to providing p99 streaming first-byte numbers in the weekly report and to propose a fallback-model mapping that will be used automatically on degraded capacity. That fallback mapping should be explicit in the SLA so our product team can validate UX impact.

Tech sync availability: Tue 23 Nov, 10:00–11:00 PT works for our SRE & product. Does that work for Marissa/Ben?

On procurement & cost: we'll need the reserved-capacity estimate by Fri 20 Nov to make the 60-day internal cycle. If you can provide the ballpark (monthly committed GPU hours + approximate cost), Ben, that will help speed this along.

Looking forward to the sync —
Carlos Montoya
VP Engineering, DataFlow Analytics
